question:
An 8-year-old boy is evaluated by a pulmonologist for a history of chronic productive cough, nasal
congestion, recurrent respiratory infections, and frequent episodes of otitis media. His parents note that
he falls ill more often than other children his age. He was born at term but required NICU care for
respiratory distress. He is fully vaccinated, including influenza, COVID-19, and the pneumococcal
13-valent conjugate vaccine (PCV13). His growth is at the 23rd percentile for height and the 12th

percentile for weight. His vital signs include a temperature of 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse of 114/min,
respirations of 29/min, blood pressure of 124/77 mmHg, and oxygen saturation of 98%. Examination
reveals bilateral middle ear effusions, nasal congestion with polyps, and diffuse rhonchi without
increased work of breathing. Laboratory work-up confirms low levels of nitrous oxide and a genetic
pulmonary disease. Which of the following interventions is most appropriate for this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Biannual chest computed tomography (CT) (B) Daily nebulized hypertonic saline (C)
Monthly immunoglobulin infusions (D) Vitamin A, D, E, K supplementation (E) Prophylactic Amoxicillin
(F) Bronchodilator therapy with albuterol (G) Long-term macrolide therapy (H) Yearly surveillance of
liver function tests (LFTs) (I) High-frequency chest wall oscillation therapy (J) Pneumococcal
polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23)
 A. Yearly surveillance of liver function tests (LFTs)
B. Bronchodilator therapy with albuterol
C. Daily nebulized hypertonic saline
D. Monthly immunoglobulin infusions
E. High-frequency chest wall oscillation therapy
F. Prophylactic Amoxicillin
G. Long-term macrolide therapy
H. Vitamin A, D, E, K supplementation
I. Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23)
J. Biannual chest computed tomography (CT)
